_comment: Configuration for tools/arifi-sync. Everything a stranger must be able to change lives here.
No path below is required to exist for `provenance`, `series`, or `recipe` to work.
`ref` is MANDATORY and MUST be the source's real default branch. Do not guess main/master:
PrismML's default branch is `prism`; resolving `prisml/master` instead silently reports a
DIFFERENT branch's head as drift. That mistake was made once during this tool's own authoring.
`pin` is the commit of that source we have actually reviewed. `currency` compares live head
against `pin`; it CANNOT be satisfied by doing nothing, because acknowledging drift requires
writing the newly-reviewed sha here.

WHAT WE TOOK IS THE ARCHITECTURAL ARGUMENT, not their benchmark: those tensors participate MULTIPLICATIVELY in the carried recurrent state of a hybrid SSM (DeltaNet / qwen3next), so quantization error compounds along the sequence instead of staying local to one matmul, and the rule that follows - multiplicative state-update participants stay f32, readouts and projections may be quantized - is checkable from the architecture rather than from a number. Their measurement (reasoning depth 17k-64k -> 33k-120k chars, structural codegen bugs eliminated on Qwen3.8-27B at tq3_4s, ~12 MiB per family) is THEIRS on THEIR hardware and is recorded as UNMEASURED on our side; no arm of it was run on this box. STILL OWED FROM THE OLDER RANGE, unchanged by this advance: afa0f398c (server RS-rollback for MTP, their 44.9 -> 61.7 tok/s claim, UNVERIFIED by us) and c8b12903e (TQ3_4S large-K rows_per_block for MTP verify batches). The pin advancing does NOT mean those landed - pin currency and capability ingestion are different axes and this file has conflated them before.

tq3.pin_review_2026_08_17_lane143: REFUTATION of this entry's own previous note, decided at CONTENT level, not sha level. tq3 has 9 branches, and sha arithmetic says master/backup/docs carry 149-185 commits 'not in tq3/main' with ~75 TQ3-mentioning subjects among them. That reading is WRONG: tq3/main is a REGRAFT (see the branch literally named backup/main-pre-regraft-20260810, 2026-08-10) onto newer upstream, so the same work carries forward under NEW shas and sha-absence is not content-absence. MEASURED: files containing TQ3_4S/TQ3_0/tq3_1s are tq3/main=54, tq3/master=53, tq3/backup=53, and the set-difference 'present in an older branch, absent from main' is EMPTY both ways. tq3/main is a STRICT SUPERSET. Spot-checks, both sha-absent and content-present in main: 5c8c26388 'ggml : fix TQ3 validation popcount on Windows' (ggml-quants.c:28/34/6947, ggml_popcount_u32) and 854516439 'llama-quant : add TQ3_4S tensor type fallback' (llama-quant.cpp:400). main additionally carries what no older branch has: 58ad80ffb perf/tq3-4s-decode-round2, afa0f398c server RS-rollback for MTP (44.9->61.7 tok/s), c8b12903e TQ3_4S large-K rows_per_block for MTP verify batches. VERDICT: port from tq3/main; the pin moves f75b55413 -> 58ad80ffb and the 'main understates' warning is retired. The 6 fork-authored commits in that range are afa0f398c, c8b12903e, 5008c268e (mtmd-cli null-model segfault + fault registry), f345912e4, 86bd2bacf (Muse Glimmer), 60102ccbf (dflash all-SWA default) - only afa0f398c is a candidate for us and it is server/MTP, not quant. NEW CONTRACT FLAGS, both filed to HQ: (A) tq3 SWAPS Q1_0 and Q2_0 - its ggml.h has Q2_0=41, Q1_0=42 against upstream's and ours Q1_0=41, Q2_0=42, and tq3 CONTRADICTS ITSELF because its own gguf-py keeps the upstream order. Geometry from its registry is Q1_0=(128,2+16) and Q2_0=(64,2+16), so a mis-tag fails loud at gguf_init, but porting this enum verbatim renumbers 41/42 and breaks the 498 tensors at id 42 in Ternary-Bonsai-27B-...-Q2_0.gguf. Port the TQ3 family onto OUR numbering; TYPE-ID-ALLOCATION.md section 3.1.1 already reserves 48/49/50/51. (B) tq3 allocates inside our reserved runtime block R: TQ3_0=200, TURBO3_0=201, TURBO4_0=202, TURBO2_0=203, COUNT=204, and its 200 is NOT our 200. Contract section 3.3 justified block R on 'no other party will ever allocate there' - that premise is now false. (C) METHOD WARNING with the longest reach: contract section 1.2 proves 'no GGUF carries a turbo id' from gguf-py registries, calling one 'the exhaustive list of type-ids their tooling can emit'. tq3 FALSIFIES that method - its gguf-py lists no TQ3_4S at all, yet lane-139's on-disk scan found 504 tensors at id 46 in the YTan file. A registry is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT; the sound test is the on-disk GGUF header scan. Full review: research/local-inference/2026-08-17-fork-delta-review.md

llama-cpp-turboquant.pin_review_2026_08_17_lane143: THE OLD PIN WAS NOT MERELY BEHIND, IT WAS ON A LINEAGE THE FORK'S HEAD NEVER TOOK. c26cbdffc is 'Merge pull request #225 from TheTom/fix-ui-assets-partial-dist' (2026-07-18). `git branch -r --contains c26cbdffc` returns exactly two refs, turboquant/fix/vulkan-turbo3-flat-dequant-241 and turboquant/tom/merge-upstream-dsv4 - it is NOT contained by feature/turboquant-kv-cache, which is what origin/HEAD resolves to. merge-base(c26cbdffc, head) = 1fd6dfe9f, an UPSTREAM UI commit from 2026-06-14, and rev-list --left-right --count gives 338/841. So any 'c26cbdffc..head = 841 commits behind' figure is divergent-history arithmetic, not a delta. Re-pinned to f6124e914 (2026-08-17). The lane-110C claim above SURVIVES the move: the TurboQuant KV/WHT surface it measured is intact at the head, so this was a stale pin, not an evaporated finding. MEASURED DELTA from the merge-base: 816 non-merge, of which 151 are fork-authored (--not upstream/master) and 33 touch turbo/TQ quant or kernels; the other ~118 are upstream sync, DeepseekV4/DSpark, UI and CI. WHAT WE TAKE, ranked. (1) 7f8302613 'ggml-cpu : declare turbo3_cpu_wht_group_size extern, not a second definition' (2026-08-07) plus follow-up c7d6442dd (2026-08-12) - NO-OP FOR US, take only for tidiness. SELF-REFUTATION, recorded because this lane first wrote the opposite and the correction is the valuable part: I initially read recut's ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp:26 `GGML_API int turbo3_cpu_wht_group_size;` as a SECOND DEFINITION in libggml-cpu against the real one in ggml-turbo-quant.c:31-32, and called it a live defect on our Windows DLL build on the strength of the fix's own commit message ('ELF interposition may merge them; two-level-namespace and DLL targets will not'). THAT WAS WRONG, and the error was not expanding the macro. In recut/2026-08-16:ggml/include/ggml.h, GGML_API expands to `... extern` in ALL FOUR branches (dllexport extern / dllimport extern / visibility-default extern / bare extern), so ops.cpp:26 is a DECLARATION on every platform and every build mode, and no second definition exists anywhere in our tree. Worse for the original framing: at turboquant's own pre-fix commit 7f8302613^ only the NON-Windows branch lacked `extern` (`__attribute__((visibility("default")))` with no extern), so their bug lived on ELF/macOS and their commit message has the platform exactly BACKWARDS - the Windows branches already carried extern. Our tree is correct as it stands; these two commits change nothing for us. (2) cd4c3a1f6 'remove the per-call mallocs from the TurboQuant vec_dot kernels' (CPU, pure win). (3) e130aef60 'close complete-audit findings - 7 port regressions + TQ4_1S dp4a kernel' (an audit of exactly the port we did). (4) The Vulkan cluster of 2026-08-03/04, our backend: 844678bf2 SET_ROWS block decomposition for turbo weight types, 160649054 TQ MUL_MAT_ID size gate limited to the f16 dequant fallback, 5f5ef77ad TQ4_1S pipeline wiring, 4f2013d66 turbo3 KV pipeline, b43efe599 turbo3 wiring correction, 353ac109e + 637300387 mul_mat_vec_id add / MUL_MAT_ID reject, b514ae496 TQ3_1S weight type, b0c39adac TQ4_1S wiring restored - our merge 70a752991 post-dates these so several are probably already in, and EACH needs a content diff before cherry-picking (per-commit tree comparison across a rebase is a build lane's job, not a register lane's). (5) f050a2501 + a70a324fa fattn-vec turbo-K split for a VGPR spill, re-gated on the LUT rather than on D - authored for HIP/CUDA, but the gating correction is architecture-general. WHAT WE SKIP AND WHY: 3243b2875 (fused TQ3_1S mul_mat on HIP gfx1100 - our rig is a 780M gfx1103 on Vulkan, not HIP), 8365224ee (CUDA-only garbage-output fix), ffc210bfb (arm64 CI), 07e01ec54 + ce3dce77b + aab782c1b (DeepseekV4/DSpark model support - a different slot), and the ~118 upstream-sync commits which arrive with the next upstream move. CONTRACT CHECK: CLEAN. This head defines TQ3_1S=45 and TQ4_1S=46, exactly the ids TYPE-ID-ALLOCATION.md section 3.1 reserves, so verbatim adoption still holds. Runtime types sit at 43/44/47. FLAG E, the one silent-capable collision in the whole contract, CONFIRMED AT THIS HEAD: TURBO2_0 is id 43 and our Q2_0_G128 is id 43, and block_turbo2_0 (ggml_half + qs[128/4] = 34 B / 128 values) is BYTE-IDENTICAL AND FIELD-IDENTICAL to block_q2_0_g128, so gguf_init's row-size check has nothing to separate them and the g128 metadata gate keys off a marker a turbo2 file would never carry - a serialized TURBO2_0 read as our g128 would dequantize wrongly and KEEP GOING (turbo2 is WHT-rotated Lloyd-Max, ours is plain scaled). THAT 'SILENT' VERDICT IS CODE-DERIVED, NOT CONTRACT-PROSE: read at recut/2026-08-16:src/llama-model-loader.cpp, llama_gguf_q2_0_g128_gate returns FALSE on `key < 0` (line 133-135) without throwing, and the only consumer is `if (q2_0_g128_enabled)` at :870 which skips the span check and llama_remap_q2_0_g128 entirely. Nothing on the false branch rejects id-43 tensors. gguf_init has already validated their spans against ggml_row_size(43) = 34 B / 128, which a turbo2_0 file matches exactly. So the file parses clean and our plain-scaled g128 kernel runs on rotated data. NOT TRIGGERED today, verified three ways at this head: no LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_TURBO2_0 in include/llama.h, no TURBO target in tools/quantize/quantize.cpp, no TURBO entry in gguf-py/gguf/constants.py. SENSITIVITY HALF, added r2 after checker finding F6 - three asserted ABSENCES are void as evidence until the query is shown able to HIT in those same files, so: all three paths exist and are non-trivial at that ref (1350 / 596 / 4973 lines), each one DOES carry the turbo family under its sibling names (LLAMA_FTYPE_MOSTLY_TQ3_1S = 43 in llama.h, a {"TQ3_1S", ...} row in quantize.cpp, TQ3_1S = 45 in constants.py), and `TURBO` is a live token elsewhere in the same tree (GGML_TYPE_TURBO2_0 = 43, GGML_OP_TURBO_WHT) - yet it returns ZERO in all three registries. The query can fire, the files are the right files, and the absence is real. Also, block_turbo2_0's in-source comment still reads '// 10 bytes total' while its static_assert computes 34 - contract section 1.1 warned about exactly those stale comments and it is still stale here. The sibling clone src/llama-cpp-turboquant is at a33ef00b1 (2026-06-23) with origin/feature/turboquant-kv-cache at fca3093c9, both OLDER than the remote head this pin now names. _comment: The recipe is recovered by DIFFING a CMakeCache against the committed snapshot, never by
grepping it. Grepping a cache for flags you already remember missed -D_WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00,
LLAMA_USE_PREBUILT_UI=OFF and -static-libgcc -static-libstdc++, and cost three failed builds.
F-085, President-ruled and BINDING: the regression judge is llama-server.
NOT llama-cli. NOT llama-bench. `binary` is not configurable to another judge on purpose.
Bench purity: reuse a binary within a comparison, never reuse a historical number,
never run timed arms under sibling load.
judge.note_no_host: --no-host is REQUIRED whenever a CPU_REPACK path is under test. Without it make_cpu_buft_list() puts the device host buffer type ahead of the CPU extra buffer types and the repack path never engages, so both A/B arms silently test the same code.
